chunks: And from them (the two), from Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said to al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'If you came to Mecca and stayed in the Haram (sanctuary).' Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'We will not make it permissible (by remaining in it) and it will not be made permissible by us (being killed in it). And to be killed on the mound of A'far is more beloved to me than to be killed in it.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically the Haram of Mecca)
key_terms.تَلِّ أَعْفَرَ: The Mound of Red Dust (referring to Karbala)
key_terms.لَا تُسْتَحَلُّ بِنَا: It is not made permissible by us (being killed in it)
key_terms.لَا نَسْتَحِلُّهَا: We do not make it permissible (by remaining)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Husayn prefer to be killed at Karbala rather than in the Haram of Mecca?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) rejects the proposal of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr to seek refuge in the Haram, asserting that his presence there would transform the sanctuary into a site of political negotiation rather than pure worship, thereby compromising its sanctity. He explicitly prefers martyrdom at 'A'far (Karbala) over death in Mecca, a choice that underscores the theological principle of maintaining the integrity of the Imam's mission and the distinctiveness of the Karbala event in Shia eschatology.
